digest.top_line: SENOMAC: 5yr RFS 89.7% vs 88.7% without completion ALND, HR 0.89 (0.66-1.19), noninferior in 1-2 SLN macromets, but 90% got nodal RT.
digest.tldr: Breast carried the day. SENOMAC clears completion ALND in cN0 pts with 1-2 sentinel macromets, and the axilla was still treated: ~90% of both arms received RT covering nodal target volumes, with 34.5% harboring non-SLN disease at dissection. Read it alongside AMAROS/OTOASOR, not Z0011.

sites.intro: Surgical de-escalation of the axilla continues to lean on nodal RT rather than replace it.

studies.name: SENOMAC
studies.tldr: 5yr RFS 89.7% vs 88.7% omitting completion ALND, HR 0.89 (0.66-1.19), noninferior in 1-2 SLN macromets.
details: 🔍 Phase 3 noninferiority RCT, 67 hospitals in 5 countries, N=2766 enrolled Jan 2015-Dec 2021; per-protocol 2540
🔍 Eligible: cN0 T1-T3, one or two sentinel-node MACROmetastases (>2mm); micromets excluded (IBCSG 23-01 settled that)
🔍 Extended eligibility vs prior trials: mastectomy allowed (36.7% / 35.7%), T3 tumors (5.5% / 6.1%), extracapsular extension allowed
📐 Noninferiority margin: upper CI bound for recurrence/death HR had to be below 1.44; observed 1.19, P<0.001
📊 Primary endpoint was OS (changed from BCSS in 2020); this report is the prespecified secondary RFS. 5yr OS 92.9% vs 92.0%, BCSS 97.1% vs 96.6%

details.text: 📊 Recurrence and death by arm (per-protocol, entire follow-up)

rows: Recurrence or death as first event

details: ☢️ 89.9% (1192/1326) SLNB-only and 88.4% (1058/1197) dissection pts got RT INCLUDING nodal target volumes. This is an RT-treated axilla, not an untreated one
☢️ RT QA: 1154 plans reviewed; eCRF matched plan in 99.3% for breast/chest wall and 96.6% for nodal target volumes. Detailed nodal level doses/volumes not yet reported
⚠️ Protocol stipulated NO specific RT target volumes or doses; national guidelines governed. Protocol-prohibited RT was therefore not even assessable
🔗 Authors state the result is comparable to AMAROS and OTOASOR (axilla treated with RT), NOT to Z0011, SINODAR-ONE or POSNOC
⚠️ Nonsentinel-node disease was NOT rare: 403/1167 (34.5%) had additional non-SLN mets at dissection; 31.3% with 1 macromet, 51.3% with 2. pN2 in 9.9% and pN3 in 3.0% of the dissection arm
⚠️ Median f/u 46.8 mo (range 1.5-94.5) with predominantly luminal disease, which recurs late; enrollment fell short of target
⚠️ ER+/HER2+ subgroup HR 0.26 (0.07-0.96) favoring SLNB only is biologically implausible as a real effect; 3 vs 10 events, one of 13 subgroups
⚠️ No clinical lymphedema measurement; arm morbidity rests on questionnaires, 3yr data for the whole population not yet available

verdict.rationale: Prespecified noninferiority met with wide margin to boundary; enrolls the mastectomy, T3 and ECE subgroups Z0011 and AMAROS excluded, resolving the residual uncertainty.
verdict.audience: cN0 T1-T3 breast, 1-2 sentinel-node macromets, planned nodal RT

studies.significance: The axilla here was irradiated, not left alone: 89.9% vs 88.4% received nodal target volumes, so this validates SLNB plus regional nodal RT, not surgical de-escalation without RT. Untreated non-SLN disease was present in 34.5%, meaning the RT field is carrying real burden. Nodal level doses and volumes are not yet reported.
studies.monday_clinic: In cN0 T1-T3 disease with one or two sentinel macrometastases, including mastectomy, T3 and extracapsular extension, this supports omitting completion dissection when regional nodal irradiation is planned; it does not speak to pts in whom nodal RT is being omitted.

primary_endpoint.name: Recurrence-free survival (prespecified secondary; primary endpoint is overall survival)

analysis_sections.label: Design
analysis_sections.body: Prospective randomized **phase 3 noninferiority** trial, 1:1, 67 hospitals in Sweden, Denmark, Germany, Greece and Italy. **2766 enrolled** Jan 2015 to Dec 2021; per-protocol population 2540 (1335 sentinel-node biopsy only, 1205 completion dissection). Median follow-up **46.8 months** (range 1.5 to 94.5).

analysis_sections.label: Population & inclusion
analysis_sections.body: **cN0, T1 to T3** breast cancer with **one or two sentinel-node macrometastases** (>2mm). Preoperative axillary ultrasound was mandatory; suspicious nonpalpable nodes were still eligible even with FNA-confirmed metastasis. Additional micrometastases and **extracapsular extension were allowed**, and both breast-conserving surgery (63.3% / 64.3%) and **mastectomy** (36.7% / 35.7%) were eligible. Mean age 61.

analysis_sections.label: Radiotherapy
analysis_sections.body: **RT including nodal target volumes was given to 89.9%** (1192/1326) of the sentinel-node-only group and 88.4% (1058/1197) of the dissection group. Whole-breast RT was mandatory after breast-conserving surgery, but the protocol **stipulated no specific target volumes or doses**, deferring to national guidelines. QA on 1154 plans showed eCRF-to-plan concordance of 99.3% for breast or chest wall and 96.6% for nodal volumes.

analysis_sections.label: Endpoints
analysis_sections.body: **Primary: overall survival** (switched from breast cancer-specific survival in 2020 on DSMB advice). Prespecified secondary endpoints were recurrence-free survival, breast cancer-specific survival and patient-reported outcomes. Noninferiority required the **upper CI bound for recurrence or death below 1.44**.

analysis_sections.label: Safety
analysis_sections.body: No clinical lymphedema measurements were performed; arm morbidity relies on the LYMPH-ICF, QLQ-C30, QLQ-BR23 and EQ-5D questionnaires at 1, 3, 5 and 10 years. Only 1-year data from a Swedish-Danish subpopulation are published; **3-year data for the whole trial are not yet available**.

analysis_sections.label: vs leading data
analysis_sections.body: Consistent with **ACOSOG Z0011** and **AMAROS**, but the authors place SENOMAC alongside **AMAROS and OTOASOR** rather than Z0011, SINODAR-ONE or POSNOC, because nodal irradiation was routine here. Where the earlier trials enrolled nearly 40% micrometastasis-only pts, one T3 patient between them, and only 248 mastectomies (17.4%) in AMAROS, SENOMAC filled each of those gaps.

analysis_sections.label: Applies to
analysis_sections.body: Represents cN0 T1 to T3 breast cancer with one or two sentinel macrometastases, including mastectomy, T3 tumors and extracapsular extension, treated with adjuvant systemic therapy and nodal irradiation per Nordic guidelines. Does not represent pts managed without regional nodal RT, men (only 10 enrolled), or micrometastasis-only disease.

analysis_sections.label: Limitations
analysis_sections.body: Detailed nodal level doses and volumes are **not yet reported**, so the RT dose actually treating the residual axilla is unquantified. Withdrawal was higher in the dissection arm, reflecting pts' wish to avoid the operation. The **ER+/HER2+ subgroup HR of 0.26 (0.07-0.96)** rests on 3 versus 10 events among 13 subgroups and should not be read as a real interaction.

analysis_sections.label: Discussion
analysis_sections.body: The completion dissection arm shows what is being left behind: **34.5% (403/1167) had additional non-sentinel-node metastases**, rising to 51.3% with two macrometastases, and 9.9% were upstaged to pN2 with 3.0% pN3. Noninferior recurrence-free survival despite that residual burden is a statement about what **systemic therapy plus nodal RT** can control, not about the axilla being clean.

studies.interpretation:
The number that governs how this trial should be read is 89.9% versus 88.4%: nearly nine in ten patients in both arms received radiotherapy that included nodal target volumes. The authors say so themselves, placing SENOMAC alongside AMAROS and OTOASOR rather than Z0011, SINODAR-ONE or POSNOC. This is not a trial of leaving a positive axilla alone. It is a trial of which modality treats it, and the answer is that regional nodal irradiation plus modern systemic therapy substitutes for dissection without a recurrence-free survival cost at five years. A reader who takes the headline as licence to omit both the dissection and the nodal fields is drawing a conclusion the trial did not test.

What SENOMAC adds over its predecessors is population, not direction. Z0011 and AMAROS both pointed this way and both were criticised for enrolling a population easier than the one in clinic: nearly 40% micrometastasis-only, one T3 patient between them, 248 mastectomies (17.4%) in AMAROS and none in Z0011, extracapsular extension either excluded or unreported. SENOMAC restricted entry to macrometastases, allowed extracapsular extension, enrolled T3 disease, and randomised more than a third of its patients to or after mastectomy. Each of those was a live source of hesitation at tumour board, and each is now covered by randomised data pointing the same way as the two trials it was designed to validate. That convergence, more than the hazard ratio itself, is what should move confidence.

The dissection arm is the trial's most instructive feature, because it quantifies what omission leaves in place. Additional non-sentinel-node metastases were found in 403 of 1167 patients (34.5%), reaching 51.3% among those with two macrometastases, and 9.9% of the dissection arm were reclassified pN2 with 3.0% pN3. Recurrence-free survival was nonetheless noninferior. The honest reading is not that this disease was absent but that it was treated, by adjuvant systemic therapy in 65% receiving chemotherapy and 93% endocrine therapy, and by the nodal fields. That framing matters for a radiation oncologist because it makes nodal coverage load-bearing rather than incidental, and the trial cannot yet say at what dose or to which levels: the detailed target-volume and dose review is explicitly still ongoing.

Two things should temper the read. Median follow-up is 46.8 months in a population that is overwhelmingly luminal, the subtype whose recurrences arrive late, so the five-year estimate is early for the biology in question and the primary endpoint of overall survival remains unreported. And the arm-morbidity case, the entire clinical rationale for de-escalating, rests here on questionnaires with no clinical lymphedema measurement and no three-year data yet for the full cohort. AMAROS supplies that piece, with lymphedema roughly twice as common after dissection as after axillary radiotherapy, but SENOMAC has not yet supplied its own.

For the result to be wrong, the non-sentinel disease left in situ would have to convert to clinical recurrence on a longer horizon than the current follow-up covers, which is precisely the failure mode a luminal population invites. The confidence interval helps, since 1.19 sits well below the 1.44 boundary and the event count rather than the missed accrual target drives precision. The ER-positive/HER2-positive subgroup HR of 0.26 (0.07-0.96) should be ignored: 3 events against 10, one of thirteen subgroups, and no mechanism by which forgoing an operation improves outcomes.

significance_by_specialty.radonc: Nodal target volumes were treated in 89.9% vs 88.4%, so the axilla was managed, not observed, and the RT field is covering the 34.5% non-sentinel-node burden the surgery would have removed. Doses and nodal levels are not yet reported, so the trial supports covering the regional nodes without specifying how.
significance_by_specialty.medonc: Systemic therapy shares the load: approximately 65% received chemotherapy and 93% endocrine therapy, and 9.9% of dissected pts were upstaged to pN2 with 3.0% pN3, meaning omission removes nodal counts that currently inform adjuvant intensity. Decisions will rest on tumour biology and genomic tools rather than final node count.
significance_by_specialty.surgonc: Completion dissection can be omitted in the subgroups the earlier trials could not answer: mastectomy (36.7%), T3 (5.5%) and extracapsular extension, with 5yr RFS 89.7% vs 88.7%. The trade is accepting known residual disease, since 34.5% of dissected pts had additional non-sentinel-node metastases and 9.9% were pN2.
